analysis_steps.goal: Select clump and core subsamples from the ALMAGAL catalog

method.value: Select ALMAGAL clumps hosting at least N_core >= 4 (514 clumps, 5728 cores) from the Coletta et al. (2025) catalog, further dividing into near (C2+C5) and far (C3+C6) groups and applying higher cuts (N_core >= 8 for mass segregation, N_core >= 10 for Q parameter).

evidence.quote: In summary, the analyzed dataset comprises 514 clumps ($N_{core}\,\geq\,4$), containing a total of 5728 cores, greatly increasing the statistics available in the literature.

In contrast, to study the global structural properties of the spatial distribution of the cores, i.e., the type of distribution, mass segregation, we restricted our analysis only to systems with a high degree of fragmentation ($N_{core}\,\geq\,8$ or higher).

validation.value: Checked that including clumps with 2 or 3 cores has a negligible impact on results

evidence.quote: The inclusion of these systems has a negligible impact on the results discussed in the paper, and the properties of their separations are consistent with the systems with $4\,\leq\,N_{cores}\,\lesssim\,6$.

analysis_steps.goal: Determine cluster centers, sizes, convex hulls, and morphological elongations

method.value: Compute cluster center via geometrical and mass-weighted average of core positions; define cluster radius R_cluster as distance of farthest core from center; construct convex hull (CH) polygon of core positions; classify systems by comparing number of hull vertices N_v^hull to interior cores N_in^hull; measure elongation via ellipse fit to CH (e_CH, PA_CH) and ratio xi = R_cluster / R^CH.

analysis_steps.goal: Quantify spatial clustering structure using the Q parameter and calibrate with synthetic clusters

method.value: Compute the Cartwright & Whitworth (2004) Q = m_bar / s_bar parameter for ALMAGAL clumps; run 1.1 million 3D synthetic cluster realizations (radial power-law p = 0, 1, 2, 2.9 and fractal box-method D = 1.5, 2.0, 2.5 for N_cores = 4 to 30, projected to 2D) to calibrate Q thresholds for small N_cores; evaluate Q vs L/M for the 226 clumps with N_cores >= 10.

evidence.quote: We defined two intervals of $Q$ where it is most likely that the cores follow a centrally concentrated ($Q\gtrsim0.8$ for high power-law exponent $p$) or subclustered distribution ($Q\lesssim0.65$, lower fractal dimension ), with a value of $Q\,=\,0.75$ that approximately separates these two regimes.

claims.hypothesis: Core separations in massive dense clumps are governed by thermal Jeans fragmentation rather than large-scale supersonic turbulence.
claims.experiment: Compare MST deprojected core separations (clump-averaged medians, modes, and full ensemble) against clump-averaged thermal Jeans lengths (lambda_J^th) calculated from Herschel dust temperatures and volume densities across 514 ALMAGAL clumps.
claims.result: Clump-averaged median and mode separations are centered at 0.91 and 0.76 times lambda_J^th (interquartile ranges 0.56-1.60 and 0.50-1.26), while a secondary population in young (L/M < 0.5-1), poorly fragmented clumps peaks at ~3 times lambda_J^th (corresponding to Mach ~ 5, still smaller than cloud-scale SEDIGISM turbulence).
claims.finding: Fragmentation in massive clumps is predominantly compatible with thermal Jeans fragmentation, with a secondary wider-separation population in young/poorly fragmented clumps that may reflect moderate local turbulent support or filament/substructure scales.

evidence.loc: ALMAGAL core separations compared to Jeans length
evidence.quote: Quantitatively, the median and the mode are centered around 0.91$\times$ and 0.76$\times$ $\lambda_{J}^{th}$, respectively.

evidence.loc: ALMAGAL core separations compared to Jeans length
evidence.quote: One of the two peaks of the distributions is centered at $R\sim1$, indicating a population of cores which are separated by a thermal Jeans length, while the second peak is shifted at higher values, which are centered at about $R\sim3$.
However, our results are compatible with thermal Jeans fragmentation being active in massive clumps.

claims.hypothesis: Typical separations between dense cores decrease as massive clumps evolve.
claims.experiment: Analyze the distribution of deprojected MST core separations and clump-averaged separations as a function of the evolutionary indicator L/M across 514 ALMAGAL clumps.
claims.result: Deprojected core separations decrease from median ~12000-18000 au (or ~20000 au) in young clumps (L/M < 1 L_sun/M_sun) to ~7300-7700 au in evolved clumps (L/M > 10 L_sun/M_sun), with Spearman rho_s = -0.37 (p << 10^-9), flattening above L/M ~ 1 L_sun/M_sun.
claims.finding: Core separations statistically decrease with clump evolution, largely driven by the transition from poorly fragmented young clumps to more crowded, highly fragmented systems as additional cores collapse and become detectable.

evidence.quote: When ALMAGAL clumps are grouped by their $L/M$ ratio, we find that the cores in more evolved systems are generally closer to one another than those in younger systems.

Similarly to the case of the entire ensemble, the averaged quantities also show a gradual decrease in the separation between the cores with $L/M$, as we determined a Spearman correlation coefficient equal to $\rho_{s} = -0.37\,[-0.38]$ for the median [mode] with a $p$-value $\ll10^{-9}$.

Although the observed trend can be statistically described by a steady decrease in these two intervals, the larger variation appears to be produced by an increase in the degree of fragmentation in more evolved systems, as more cores are detected.

claims.hypothesis: Dense core distributions progressively transition from fractal subclustering to smooth, centrally concentrated configurations as clumps evolve.
claims.experiment: Calibrate the Cartwright & Whitworth (2004) Q parameter using 1.1M synthetic clusters and measure Q as a function of L/M for 226 ALMAGAL clumps hosting N_cores >= 10.
claims.result: Young clumps (L/M <= 2) are mainly fractal/subclustered (13 with Q < 0.65, only 4 with Q > 0.8), and centrally concentrated systems (Q > 0.8) are more frequent at later stages, but Q shows large scatter at all L/M with very weak correlation (Pearson rho_p = 0.18, Spearman rho_s = 0.185) and 27 of 124 evolved clumps (L/M > 10) still have Q < 0.65.
claims.finding: There is no robust progressive transition from fractal subclustering to centrally concentrated patterns governed solely by internal clump evolution (L/M); subclustering frequently persists into advanced stages.

evidence.quote: The ALMAGAL cores are typically distributed in fractal-type subclusters, while centrally concentrated patterns appear only at later stages, but we do not observe a progressive transition between these configurations with evolution.

A weak dependence of $Q$ with the $L/M$ ratio may be identified, but the Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients equal to $\rho_{p}$ = 0.18 and $\rho_{s}$ = 0.185 with $p$-values of 0.0067 and 0.0053 are significantly lower than the values reported by (cite: Xu2024): $\rho_{p}$ = 0.60 and $\rho_{s}$ = 0.57.

claims.hypothesis: Mass segregation of dense cores is present prior to gas dispersal and increases in occurrence and strength as clumps evolve.
claims.experiment: Compute the mass segregation ratio Lambda_MSR(N_MST) with 500 Monte Carlo mass-uncertainty realizations for 296 ALMAGAL clumps with N_cores >= 8 across three L/M intervals.
claims.result: 110 of 296 clumps (~37%) show robust mass segregation (>70% MC probability); the occurrence rises from ~17% (10/59) for L/M < 2, to 30% (25/83) for 2 < L/M <= 10, to ~49% (75/154) for L/M > 10 L_sun/M_sun, while median Lambda_MST^max increases from ~5 to ~6.2-6.4.
claims.finding: Mass segregation can be present at early stages but becomes nearly three times more common and more pronounced as massive clumps evolve.

evidence.quote: In conclusion, although MS may be present in the earliest stages, it is about three times more common in evolved clumps ($L/M\,>\,10$ L$_{\odot}$/M$_{\odot}$).

why_this_data.value: The ALMAGAL survey provides a large, homogeneous sample of 1013 clumps observed at matched ~1000 au physical resolution across a wide range of masses, surface densities, and evolutionary stages (L/M), overcoming small sample sizes and heterogeneous resolutions/sensitivities of previous surveys.

evidence.quote: The ALMA Cycle 7 large program ALMA evolutionary study of high-mass protocluster formation in the GALaxy (ALMAGAL) (2019.1.00195L, P.I.: S.Molinari, P.Schilke, C.Battersby, and P.Ho) was designed to mitigate these problems by observing an unprecedented large sample of 1013 clumps covering a wide range of physical conditions and Galactic locations (cite: Molinari2025).

why_this_method.value: Minimum spanning tree (MST) edge lengths directly trace nearest-neighbor fragmentation scales without requiring the full distance matrix; analyzing both clump-averaged estimators (median and KDE mode) and the stacked ensemble preserves information from poorly fragmented clumps while characterizing multi-modal separation distributions; Q and Lambda_MSR quantify subclustering vs central concentration and mass segregation.

evidence.quote: In this work, we do not require the complete information provided by $\delta(i,j)$, as, to describe the length of fragmentation, it is sufficient to relate each core to its direct neighbor. Those separation are usually computed with the minimum spanning tree (MST) method.
These two approaches allow for a well-rounded and complete description of the statistical information present in our measurements and to determine the possible link to the clump-averaged properties.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Measuring extended clump sizes directly on ALMAGAL interferometric continuum images was rejected because spatial filtering misses significant extended flux; Herschel 250 um CuTEx sizes R_cl were used instead.

evidence.quote: However, as discussed by (cite: Molinari2025), ALMAGAL interferometric data are affected by spatial filtering, and in several fields, they may miss a significant flux fraction. This makes ALMAGAL data unsuitable for reliably tracing the full, extended emission of the clump, even if they reveal the complexity of the clump inner structure.

referee_caveats_inferred: Deprojection uses a constant statistical factor (4/pi) assuming isotropic 3D random orientation, whereas cores in flattened hubs or filaments have anisotropic 3D geometries that can bias deprojected lengths.

Apparent evolutionary decrease in MST separation with L/M is strongly coupled to the increase in detected core number N_cores with L/M (higher contrast/luminosity cores becoming detectable above the flux limit) rather than purely dynamical shrinking of core positions.
